continuous_text.content:
I think that we all should
Try to do something good.

We have a lot to share.

I want to do what's right.
I think we really could
Show respect, not neglect.
We'll feel good!

continuous_text.title: Isabel's Journal
continuous_text.content:
September 7, 20__
Starting now, I am going to write about kindness. I think that kind acts show a person's character. For example, yesterday my friend Eileen forgot her lunch. Kevin gave her half of his sandwich and a piece of cake that he had planned to save for later.
Sometimes, it takes courage to do what is right. Today on the playground, kids started teasing a girl in my class named Lisa. She was afraid. Eileen made a hard choice. She could have ignored them, but she told them to stop it right now! I know it was hard for her to go against a crowd. The other kids listened, though, and stopped being mean. I think that Kevin and Eileen both have excellent characters.

continuous_text.title: Are You a Good Citizen?
continuous_text.content:
Are you a good citizen at school? Do you feel you have a good character? Think about it. Are you kind to other students? Do you respect their ideas? Do you hear what they have to say? Are you thoughtful of other students' feelings? A good citizen cheers for others. Sometimes it takes courage to do the right thing. Can you do that? Do you follow school rules and help others follow the rules, too?
A good citizen does these things all year. If this sounds like you, it's clear you are a good citizen. Other students will be happy to have you as a friend. Your teacher will be happy to have you in the class, too.

continuous_text.title: The Lion and the Mouse
continuous_text.content:
[Structural Summary & Key Excerpts]
Setting: A forest. A tiny mouse accidentally runs past a sleeping lion.
Action: The lion traps the mouse under his paw. The mouse fearfully begs for mercy, saying 'Spare me, and maybe I could help you someday.' The lion laughs at the idea but generously frees her.
Climax: Hunters trap the lion in a net. The mouse hears him and quickly chews a hole in the net to set him free.
Moral: 'Great help can come from small friends.'
continuous_text.speaker_structure: Dialogue between Lion and Mouse; Narrator
continuous_text.notes: Aesop fable adapted by Shirleyann Costigan. Excerpted/summarized structurally to preserve curriculum evidence without triggering automated recitation filter blocks.

continuous_text.title: The Farmer and the Eagle
continuous_text.content:
[Structural Summary & Key Excerpts]
Setting: Farmer Bean's barn and field.
Action: Farmer Bean finds an eagle caught in a mousetrap. He gently frees the eagle, who flies away.
Climax: That afternoon, Farmer Bean sits beside a stone wall to eat lunch. The eagle swoops down and takes his hat. Farmer Bean chases the eagle across the field to get his hat back.
Resolution: While chasing the hat, the wall collapses and crushes his lunch spot. The eagle's actions saved his life.
Moral: 'Help can come from unexpected places.'
continuous_text.notes: Aesop fable adapted by Shirleyann Costigan. Excerpted/summarized structurally to preserve curriculum evidence without triggering automated recitation filter blocks.

continuous_text.title: Meet the Legend: Aesop
continuous_text.content:
"Aesop's Fables" are a collection of very famous, very old stories. They are called "Aesop's Fables" because many people believe they were written by a man from ancient Greece named Aesop. Aesop told wise stories that used animals to teach lessons about people. People say that Aesop was a slave, but he was such a wonderful storyteller that his master set him free.
Today, "Aesop's Fables" are some of the most famous stories in the world.

continuous_text.title: Wisdom of the Ages
continuous_text.content:
Proverbs can help us remember to do our very best. What do these proverbs say about helping others?

"If the heart is good, the deeds will be good." — Japanese proverb

"Today is my turn, and tomorrow is your turn." — Samoan proverb

"Someone who gives to me, teaches me to give." — Danish proverb

"Do good deeds and don't worry about who deserves them." — Mexican proverb

"To give quickly is a great virtue." — Hindu proverb

"Good actions are not lost." — Turkish proverb

"Do a good deed and then do it again." — Welsh proverb
continuous_text.notes: Proverbs from around the world across pages 239-241.
